brief: What VCs don't tell solo founders. The dilution math, the rollup risk, the optionality you give up the moment you sign.

slots.scriptTagline: The term sheet locks the door behind you.

slots.body: Seed rounds slice you in half. Series A and B halve you again. By the exit, you own single digits while carrying all the risk.
Two independent seats sound fair until they fire you. VCs vote as a bloc. Your company becomes their asset, not your life.
Most exits are acqui-hires or feature rollups. Your product dies inside a suite. You get handcuffed for three years while they strip the code.
Preferred stock blocks side exits and small sales. You cannot sell for ten million even if it saves your sanity. The spreadsheet decides.
You hire fast and spend faster to chase unicorn metrics. Profits become poison. You trade a calm business for a stressful valuation story.
Customers dilute nothing. Retained profit buys your freedom. You can still sell later, but on your timeline and your terms, not theirs.

slots.headline: RECLAIM YOUR CAP TABLE
slots.scriptTagline: Profit is the only term sheet left.
